documents.author: Dr. Helen Brooks
documents.text: Admitted with hyperglycemia (glucose 412 mg/dL) and acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease stage 3. History of type 2 diabetes mellitus for 18 years, hypertension. Treated with IV fluids and insulin infusion, transitioned to basal-bolus insulin. Creatinine improved from 2.4 to 1.7 mg/dL. Metformin discontinued due to eGFR below 30. Discharged home with glucose meter teaching. Follow up with nephrology in 2 weeks.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: IMPRESSION: Bilateral echogenic kidneys consistent with medical renal disease. Right kidney 9.1 cm, left kidney 9.4 cm. No hydronephrosis. No renal calculi.

documents.author: Dr. Priya Natarajan, Nephrology
documents.text: Nephrology consult for CKD stage 3b with recent AKI. Diabetic nephropathy suspected; urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 480 mg/g. Started empagliflozin is deferred until eGFR stabilizes. Recommend ACE inhibitor titration and repeat BMP in 1 week. Avoid NSAIDs.

documents.author: Dr. Priya Natarajan, Nephrology
documents.text: Nephrology consult for CKD stage 3b with recent AKI. Diabetic nephropathy suspected; urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 480 mg/g. Started empagliflozin is deferred until eGFR stabilizes. Recommend ACE inhibitor titration and repeat BMP in 1 week. Avoid NSAIDs.

documents.author: Dr. Karen Liu, Emergency Medicine
documents.text: 53-year-old male with 2 hours of substernal chest pressure radiating to left arm, diaphoresis. ECG shows 2 mm ST depression in V4-V6. Initial high-sensitivity troponin 88 ng/L, repeat 240 ng/L. Diagnosis: NSTEMI. Aspirin, heparin drip, atorvastatin 80 mg started. Cardiology consulted for catheterization.

documents.author: Dr. Marcus Feld, Interventional Cardiology
documents.text: Left heart catheterization: 90% stenosis of proximal left anterior descending artery, treated with one drug-eluting stent with TIMI 3 flow. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated 45%. Recommend dual antiplatelet therapy for 12 months.

documents.author: Dr. Marcus Feld
documents.text: Transthoracic echocardiogram: LVEF 45% with hypokinesis of the anterior wall and apex. Mild mitral regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.

documents.author: Dr. Omar Haddad
documents.text: Moderate persistent asthma with acute exacerbation after viral URI. SpO2 91% on room air, diffuse expiratory wheeze. Peak flow 45% predicted. Treated with nebulized albuterol and ipratropium x3, oral prednisone 40 mg. Improved to SpO2 96%. Discharged on 5-day prednisone burst and step-up to medium-dose ICS-formoterol.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: PA and lateral chest radiograph. Hyperinflated lungs. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. IMPRESSION: Findings compatible with reactive airway disease. No pneumonia.

documents.author: Dr. Helen Brooks
documents.text: Admitted for acute decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 25%). Presented with orthopnea, 4 kg weight gain and bilateral leg edema. NT-proBNP 6,800 pg/mL. Diuresed with IV furosemide, net negative 5.2 L. Started sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone. Atrial fibrillation rate controlled with metoprolol; apixaban continued. Discharge weight 81 kg. Fluid restriction 1.5 L/day.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: Portable AP chest. Cardiomegaly with cephalization of pulmonary vasculature, bilateral interstitial edema and small bilateral pleural effusions. IMPRESSION: Pulmonary edema.

documents.author: Dr. Ana Petrov, Cardiology
documents.text: Heart failure clinic follow-up. NYHA class II, weight stable at 80 kg. No orthopnea. Potassium 5.4 mmol/L on spironolactone - dose reduced to 12.5 mg. Continue sacubitril-valsartan. Referred for ICD evaluation if LVEF remains below 35% at 3 months.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: MRI brain with and without contrast. No acute infarct, mass or hemorrhage. No abnormal enhancement. IMPRESSION: Normal MRI of the brain.

documents.author: Dr. Lena Fischer, Neurology
documents.text: Chronic migraine without aura, 16 headache days per month, medication overuse with ibuprofen. Neurological exam normal; MRI brain normal. Started topiramate 25 mg nightly, titrate to 50 mg. Counseled on limiting analgesics to fewer than 10 days per month.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening. 30 pack-year smoker. Centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant. 9 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe. Lung-RADS 4A. IMPRESSION: Suspicious pulmonary nodule; recommend 3-month follow-up low-dose CT.

documents.author: Dr. Rafael Ortiz, Pulmonology
documents.text: COPD GOLD 2, FEV1 62% predicted. Continue tiotropium. Discussed RUL nodule found on screening CT; plan repeat CT in 3 months versus PET-CT. Smoking cessation counseling, started varenicline.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: Follow-up CT chest. The right upper lobe nodule has grown from 9 mm to 13 mm with new spiculated margins. Lung-RADS 4B. IMPRESSION: Interval growth, highly suspicious for malignancy. Recommend PET-CT and tissue sampling.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Dilated appendix measuring 12 mm with periappendiceal fat stranding and an appendicolith. No abscess or free air. IMPRESSION: Acute appendicitis.

documents.author: Dr. Nina Alvarez, General Surgery
documents.text: Procedure: Laparoscopic appendectomy. Findings: inflamed, non-perforated appendix. Estimated blood loss 10 mL. No complications. Patient tolerated the procedure well.

documents.author: Dr. Nina Alvarez
documents.text: Uncomplicated laparoscopic appendectomy for acute appendicitis. Tolerating diet, pain controlled with acetaminophen. Discharged postoperative day 1. Return precautions for fever or worsening abdominal pain.

documents.author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka, Breast Imaging
documents.text: Diagnostic mammogram, left breast. 1.8 cm irregular spiculated mass at 2 o'clock with associated pleomorphic microcalcifications. BI-RADS 4C: high suspicion for malignancy. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy recommended.

documents.author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka, Breast Imaging
documents.text: Targeted left breast ultrasound: 1.7 x 1.4 cm hypoechoic irregular mass with angular margins at 2 o'clock, 4 cm from the nipple. One borderline left axillary lymph node with cortical thickening of 3.5 mm.

documents.author: Dr. Victor Hale, Pathology
documents.text: Left breast, 2 o'clock, core needle biopsy: invasive ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade 2. Estrogen receptor positive (95%), progesterone receptor positive (60%), HER2 negative (IHC 1+). Ki-67 20%.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: Non-contrast CT head. No intracranial hemorrhage. Subtle loss of gray-white differentiation in the left insular cortex. IMPRESSION: Findings concerning for early left MCA territory ischemic stroke.

documents.author: Dr. Samuel Reyes, Radiology
documents.text: MRI brain: restricted diffusion in the left frontal operculum and insula consistent with acute infarct. Moderate chronic small vessel ischemic disease. MRA: severe stenosis of the left internal carotid artery origin.

documents.author: Dr. Lena Fischer, Neurology
documents.text: Acute left MCA ischemic stroke presenting with expressive aphasia and right arm weakness. Received IV tenecteplase within 3 hours. NIHSS improved from 8 to 3. Left ICA stenosis 80% on carotid duplex; vascular surgery planning carotid endarterectomy. Started aspirin, clopidogrel for 21 days and high-intensity statin. Outpatient speech therapy.
